mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases do not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases do not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST declines do not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances following a decrease in FEDFUNDS, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and subsequent SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increases do not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO declines do not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase simultaneously by more than 1% and 200,000 respectively in a month, it signals strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and PAYEMS > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in RSAFS and PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-interest-rate environment (FEDFUNDS < 2%), an increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
